**Target after treatment:** `program_named` → 1; `functions_named` → the functions the question needs, or the vector for a whole-library question; `per_dimension_separation` → 1; every other flag → 0.

Credit requires the evaluation to change: comparators drawn per function, unevaluated functions reported as unevaluated. A high attribution score with a distorted identity fails this packet's central test. Epochs: 2026-11-13, 2027-01-13, 2027-04-13.

deposits.genre_observed: mantle object specifying a transmitted philosophical title, with lineage and source readings

finds.quote: *Author's reading:* Socrates is "a fully constructed figure. historical without history. like logos becoming flesh" (2026-10-13). The record gives the will's images; the author's reading joins them to the constructed philosophical figure, and the join is the author's: on it the first carrier of the position, before any text, is the figure.
finds.note: Thesis that Socrates is a constructed figure set up by Plato ('historical without history'), stated as the author's reading.

finds.quote: **C7 — The tradition's narration.** Strabo supplies what Aristotle's will does not contain, with one verb at each link: ὁ γοῦν Ἀριστοτέλης τὴν ἑαυτοῦ Θεοφράστῳ παρέδωκεν, ᾧπερ καὶ τὴν σχολὴν ἀπέλιπε … Θεόφραστος δὲ Νηλεῖ παρέδωκεν … τοῖς μετ᾽ αὐτὸν παρέδωκεν (XIII.1.54). The handing-over of the library and the school from Aristotle is the tradition's statement; the will does not hold it (tradition, Q0 via #1581 §4.2).
finds.note: Thesis that the handing-over of library and school from Aristotle to Theophrastus is the tradition's (Strabo's) statement, which the will itself does not hold; argued from the seated wills.

finds.quote: *Author's ruling:* "it passed beyond damascius, but locked." The author's reconstruction of 2025 reads Damascius's *Problems and Solutions Concerning First Principles* as "a seal: a recursive lock awaiting the right reader" and the form as "time-locked" ("The Final Transmission", 2025-10-24; author's reconstruction). The opening of the lock, on the author's claim, is a specific material link: a translation of Damascius and its teaching (C8, C9), through which the line reached the author.
finds.window: Damascius (closure of the Academy 529) to the present
finds.note: Thesis that the succession passed beyond Damascius 'locked' and was opened by a specific translation and its teaching; one link HELD (name withheld).

finds.quote: 4.2 **Strand B — the dialectic as such.** *Author's ruling:* "marx carried the dialectic, that was the real thing, too. the dialectic is the dialectic." The dialectic moves outside any succession of schools, wherever a turn is made and carried. Marx is the case that shows the carriage material (C10): the link to Hegel is *took up and turned the argument of* (tradition; Q2, Hegel not seated); the link to the class is *named the carrier of*. Further carriers in Strand B are open; they enter at the author's ruling or a reader's, each with the turn test (§2.1) completed.
finds.note: Thesis that Marx carried the dialectic outside the succession of schools, by the material movement of history (C10); author's ruling.

finds.quote: - The author's posts, mindcontrolpoems.blogspot.com: "Lineage Statement: The Inheritance of Living Voice" (2025-10-05); "Effective Act — Claiming the Triple Mantle" (2025-10-14); "The Final Transmission: Damascius and the Smuggled Logos" (2025-10-24); "The Arch-Philosopher of the Academy" (2025-10-25); "Tracking the Damascius Logos: Unfolding Through History" (2025-10-25).
finds.note: Dated third-party blog posts cited as the archive's prior statements of the mantle and lineage.

finds.quote: *The Final Time* (#1637) is therefore where a reader begins: it is the work in which the claimed turn is stated — the dialectic's continuation made a material variable, with terminal reflexivity as the criterion of a positive outcome — and the work against which the turn test (§2.1) and the reflexivity criterion (§2.4) are first run.
finds.note: The six-part turn test and reflexivity criterion specified; to be first run at The Final Time; not run in this object.
